A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Reason-RFT framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, training-efficiency measurements, reward ablations and comparisons of CoT activation datasets.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds backbone comparisons, general-benchmark evaluations, CoT-quality measurements and a data-quality audit.

M1.justification: The CoT-SFT initialization, GRPO reinforcement stage, format and accuracy rewards, and structured outputs are retained. Appendix D expands documentation of CoT construction without establishing a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Appendix C and Table 7 add evaluation on MMMU, RealWorldQA, MathVision and AI2D, substantially broadening quantitative coverage. The counting subsets DS-D and DS-M are renamed versions of the Encountered and UnEncountered subsets already evaluated in v1 Table 2.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 removes LLaVA-OneVision-7B, which v1 evaluated on all three core tasks. The remaining main comparison models and the ANS-SFT, CoT-SFT and Reason-RFT-Zero paradigms are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds training comparisons on Qwen2.5-VL-3B and InternVL3-2B and an n=100 CoT evaluation using reasoning-step and lexical metrics. Appendix B changes structure-perception training from six to five epochs without establishing reruns. Table 1 also changes counting aggregation from ID/pooled-OOD averaging to ID/DS-D/DS-M averaging.

E4.justification: Appendices C, D and F add analyses of backbone robustness, general-capability retention, CoT quality and curation errors. Existing reward and mixed-CoT ablations remain. The brief v1 finding about restricting inference reasoning length is removed; the qualitative case examples are retained and rearranged.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 in v3 newly states that accuracy is averaged across five training seeds; v1 does not disclose a run count. This does not establish an increase in runs, and corresponding confidence intervals or significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: Tables 6, 7 and 9 add substantial backbone, general-benchmark and CoT-quality results. Appendix D newly reports critical CoT errors falling from approximately 3.8% to below 1% after verification. Most original scores remain unchanged, but Table 1 changes the 7B Reason-RFT-Zero spatial AVG from 56.68 to 60.34; counting averages and rankings also change through reaggregation.

T1.justification: Appendix D newly defines a task-specific target CoT length using equally weighted human and model mean lengths, with an acceptance interval of 0.6 to 1.4 times that target. The core SFT, GRPO and reward equations remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central framework and its three claimed benefits remain, but v3 asserts priority as the first such framework and focuses generalization claims on domain shift. The introduction changes its efficiency headline from over 95% of SFT performance using under 20% of the data to over 90% using under 5%.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations about backbone-independent benefits, preservation of general capabilities and RL improving CoT coherence and self-checking. Appendix H identifies larger models and complex real-world applications as future validation needs. The general-capability interpretation is overstated because Table 7 includes declines relative to zero-shot performance.

D1.justification: New Table 4 specifies stage-specific learning rates, batches, trainable parameters, optimizers, sequence limits and completion counts. Appendices D and E document CoT prompting, sampling, filtering, manual verification, and the sources and sample counts of existing mixed-CoT datasets. These substantially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands citations across vision, robotics, transformation reasoning and benchmarks, including RoboBrain 2.0, RoboOS, VisualTrans, MMMU and graph/puzzle datasets, while removing LLaVA-OneVision. It also strengthens positioning from adapting R1 methods to VLMs to claiming the first such adaptation.

P1.justification: Existing abstract, introduction, methodological explanations and results discussions are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized around five research questions, the mixed-CoT ablation moves to Appendix C, and the appendix gains separate construction, quality-analysis and limitations sections.

P2.justification: The paper switches from two-column formatting to a single-column NeurIPS layout, combines earlier counting summaries into Table 1, and adds configuration and evaluation tables. Figures are resized and rearranged; several existing structure-perception examples are relabeled as general visual reasoning.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v3 provides substantially more useful implementation documentation and broader empirical checks through Tables 4, 6 and 7 and Appendices D–F. The net benefit is limited by overinterpretation and a narrowed comparator set: Appendix C claims no general-benchmark degradation despite 2B RealWorldQA scoring 53.06 versus 61.31 zero-shot, while the strong LLaVA-OneVision comparator is removed.
